note: A HELD STAGE ROW IS NOT SUPERSEDED BY A LATER MERGE, AND THE REASON IS KIND, NOT STATE. campaign/the-ken currently shows two rows: req-6e9c2456dce5 held/stage (refused at the mouth, conflicts against e3f47eb47) and req-a0a4e38e6634 running/merge. They look contradictory and are not. The held row sits on 6e9c2456d, an ancestor from before the campaign absorbed main at 851ad1cdb; the branch is now 0 behind main and git merge origin/main reports Already up to date, so those conflicts are real for that old SHA and cannot recur on the current one. THE COALESCING RULE, read from sluice-queue.sh rather than remembered: supersedable is queued OR held -- held IS supersedable, and a comment there explains why (a held request is one the chamber reddened, so the descendant IS the replacement). What blocks it is the very next clause, rkind = kind. A merge request never supersedes a stage request, whatever their ancestry. So a campaign that stage-gates, absorbs, then submits a merge will always leave its stage row held forever unless a human drops it, and no make target exposes a manual state verb. Worth knowing before reading a held row as a live problem: check kind before checking ancestry. I am leaving the row for the operator to drop; the merge is unaffected and running.
